fact: Biometric Update, citing SOS Media Burundi, says refugees in camps and urban areas are being enrolled in Rwanda's national biometric ID registration drive, with face, fingerprint and iris captured.
Biometric Update, citing SOS Media Burundi, says refugees who have received their ID cards have been able to open bank accounts and buy SIM cards.

The New Times says the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration began on 7 February 2026 an electronic ID card registration for refugees, asylum seekers, migrants and stateless persons in Kigali, with identity verification and biometric capture, running to 15 February.

fact: NIDA says the national digital ID registration exercise covers refugees, with camp refugees registering at camp level and urban refugees at sector or cell offices, on presenting a refugee ID or proof of registration.
NIDA says registration and photography for the digital ID, which includes refugees, began on 28 October 2025 and reaches Kigali from 7 February 2026, with issuance planned from June 2026.
NIDA's Director General says the new digital ID will include groups previously left out, such as asylum seekers and stateless persons in border areas.

MINEMA, citing the Government's GRF pledge updates, says 93% of eligible refugees in Rwanda have been issued refugee identity cards and 99% of refugees born in Rwanda have had their births registered, with nearly 140,000 refugees hosted.

Immigration, with the refugee ministry and UNHCR, is running a registration campaign in all refugee camps and urban centres to issue refugees the new biometric ID cards; a large share at Mahama (over 70,000 refugees) is already registered.
A Kigali urban refugee says that with the earlier refugee ID cards they could open bank accounts and buy SIM cards.

Access to Finance Rwanda says Rwanda's integration of refugees and asylum seekers into the national identification system has made it easier for them to open bank accounts and access financial services.
The FinScope 2024 refugees report, presented by Access to Finance Rwanda, says 76 percent of adult refugees own registered mobile money accounts and 37 percent use bank accounts.
